repository.label: Identify discs
repository.description: Finds the PlayStation 2 images in baserom/ and checks each one's size and SHA-1 against games/*/game.json.

repository.label: Verify every checksum
repository.description: The same, with every checksum game.json lists (CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256). Reads each 4 GB image several times: minutes, not seconds.

repository.label: Place inputs
repository.description: Puts what each game's build reads where it expects it: hard links to your images, boot executables read out of them, links to toolchains/. Never overwrites a file.

repository.label: Test OpenRAC's tools
repository.description: The unit tests of tools/ (no disc or toolchain needed).

repository.label: Update OpenRAC
repository.description: Brings the checkout up to date with the published OpenRAC.
repository.todo: Decide how players get updates: git pull in a checkout (refuse when the tree has local changes) or a bundled release of the tools. See docs/INTEGRATION.md, 'Open decisions'.

rac1/pal.label: Extract the assembly
rac1/pal.description: Splits the boot executable and the 19 level programs into assembly with splat.

rac1/pal.label: Build the PS2 program
rac1/pal.description: Compiles the decompiled C with SN ProDG and links the executable.

rac1/pal.label: Preview a level in Godot
rac1/pal.description: Opens one extracted level in Godot's player, to fly around it. This is Godot showing the editor's scene, not the game.

rac1/pal.label: Check the progress report
rac1/pal.description: Recomputes progress/report.json from the source and compares it with the committed one, as CI does. Needs neither disc nor toolchain.

rac1/pal.label: Extract the levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the 19 levels on your disc into Godot 4 projects, one per level, in assets/levels/rac1/pal. About 20 seconds and 800 MB. Run it again to add levels or bring them up to date: levels you edited are kept, and one made by an older editor is backed up with your edits before it is written again.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS the same command wrote the per-level projects, and refused an existing folder with a clear message.

rac1/pal.label: Import a level into Godot
rac1/pal.description: Has Godot read one level's meshes and textures without opening a window. Not needed before opening the editor, which does the same the first time (a few seconds per level).
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS, Godot 4.7.2 imported one extracted level this way in five seconds; a 4.9 development build crashed on it.

rac1/pal.label: Open a level in Godot
rac1/pal.description: Opens one level in the Godot editor: move, turn or scale its objects and save. Each level is a project of its own, so only that level loads.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. The project file is assets/godot/project.godot, as the action expects.

rac1/pal.label: Pack your edited levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the levels you edited in Godot back into the game's level data, in assets/packed/rac1/pal; your disc image is never changed. Packs the objects you moved, turned, scaled, changed, added or deleted.
rac1/pal.todo: Run from a shell on macOS: an untouched project packs to nothing, a scene Godot re-saved with one object moved packs to a level file that differs from the disc in that object's record, and the port ran level 0 for 400 frames from it. Not run from the desktop app yet. Next: adding and deleting objects, then ties and shrubs.

rac1/pal.label: Test the level editor
rac1/pal.description: The unit tests of editor/ (no disc needed).
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS: 66 tests, OK.

rac1/pal.label: Build the game
rac1/pal.description: Compiles the decompiled game for this computer with the compilers it finds (on Windows, Visual Studio's C++ tools, Clang and Ninja). A few minutes the first time; later builds redo only what changed.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app on each platform. tools/build_port.py ran from a shell on Windows 11 (Visual Studio 2026, Clang 21): an incremental build, a rerun of hostgen, nothing to do. Another copy of the decompilation is chosen once, with tools/build_port.py --source DIR; the launcher has no setting for it yet.

rac1/pal.label: Rebuild the game from scratch
rac1/pal.description: Deletes everything built before and compiles the game again from the start, keeping the decompilation and disc it was built from. The launcher does this after an update, when the game was built by an older OpenRAC. A few minutes.

rac1/pal.label: Get the levels ready
rac1/pal.description: Reads the levels from your disc into the form the game draws: the worlds behind the menus and all 19 levels, in assets/port/rac1/pal. About half a minute and 1 GB, once.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. The same command from a shell on macOS wrote what the port draws from. --replace: run again, it puts a new export in the old one's place once the new one is whole.

rac1/pal.label: Add the levels' visibility
rac1/pal.description: Adds the game's own record of what can be seen from each spot to levels read before OpenRAC kept it, so the game draws only what you can see. A few seconds, from your disc, once.

needs.from: the levels (Get the levels ready)

rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. The Vulkan renderer culls with it (docs/port/RENDERER.md); OpenGL keeps its own visibility. editor/extract.py port writes the stamp itself, so a fresh export needs nothing more (2026-10-22).

rac1/pal.label: Check the levels
rac1/pal.description: The game reads every level as it will when you play, without opening its window, and says which it cannot draw. A few seconds. Play waits for it: a level that is missing or cut short would be a black world.

needs.from: the levels (Get the levels ready)

rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS it passed a whole export (21 levels) and named the two levels of one with a folder removed and a file emptied.

rac1/pal.label: Prepare the enhanced lighting
rac1/pal.description: Bakes the light that bounces off each level, for Enhanced graphics (Mods), from your own extracted levels: one level per CPU thread, each kept until the levels are read again. A few minutes, once.

needs.from: a check of the levels (Check the levels)

rac1/pal.todo: Run from the Mods tab's Enhanced graphics. From a shell on macOS bake_all.py --update baked a PAL level in 46 s; --disc is only read for exports made before the bake inputs.

rac1/pal.label: Play
rac1/pal.description: The game as a native PC program: its decompiled C built for this computer, drawn by OpenRAC's own renderer, with the assets from your disc.
rac1/pal.todo: Built by port-build. The port reads each level's program from your disc image when decompiler_out (openrac-extractor --decompile) is not there. It draws from the levels port-levels writes (--levels): without them the menus have no world behind them and a level has no scenery. Runs on Windows, Linux and macOS: the port is one program for all three (it was listed for Windows and Linux only until 2026-10-13, though it had been built and run on macOS).

rac1/pal.label: Export models and textures
rac1/pal.description: Writes a level's models (glTF, with their skeletons and animations) or textures (PNG) to a folder of their own, to open in Blender or an image editor. A few seconds.

needs.from: the levels (Get the levels ready)

rac1/pal.label: Import your edits
rac1/pal.description: Reads an export you edited back: what changed becomes an overrides pack, checked against the game's skeletons and texture shapes. Your levels and the export are never changed.

needs.from: the levels (Get the levels ready)

rac1/pal.label: Add an overrides pack
rac1/pal.description: Copies a pack (a .zip or a folder with openrac-mod.json) into the game's mods, after checking it. The file you chose is never changed.

rac1/pal.label: Put the mods together

rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS a 4x terrain texture showed at its size in Godot 4.7.2 after the import.
